dedupe_keys.name: simulation based methodology to identify relevant damage indicators and safety thresholds for post earthquake evaluation of structures

description: Simulation-Based Methodology to Identify Relevant Damage Indicators and Safety Thresholds for Post-Earthquake Evaluation of Structures is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Gregory Deierlein, Stanford University (stanford.edu). After a strong earthquake, criteria are needed to determine whether buildings are safe to reoccupy based on observable damage. This paper presents a simulation-based methodology to identify relevant damage indicators and safety thresholds for building structures. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: post-earthquake safety, damage indicators, tagging, reinforced concrete frames. Published 2023-01-04. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
